Take this free CAT Mixtures and Alligations online test — 10 exam-pattern MCQs with instant scoring and a worked explanation for every answer. The Mixtures & Alligations chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Mixtures & Alligations tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Mixtures & Alligations

The alligation rule, repeated replacement of liquid, and multi-ingredient mixing to a target price or concentration.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • Alligation: (cheaper qty)/(dearer qty) = (dearer − mean)/(mean − cheaper).
  • After n replacements of x from V: pure left = V(1 − x/V)ⁿ.
  • Mixing prices c, d in ratio m:n gives mean = (mc + nd)/(m+n).

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Swapping the numerator and denominator in the alligation rule.
  • Using arithmetic (not the (1−x/V)ⁿ formula) for repeated replacement.
  • Mixing quantities measured in different units.

faq.a: Whenever two things at different rates/concentrations are mixed to a known average — it gives the mixing ratio in one step.
If x litres are removed and replaced with water n times from a V-litre vessel, pure liquid left = V(1 − x/V)ⁿ.
